correctness.rationale: For each integer exponent the finite triangular Fourier spectrum remains nonnegative under discrete convolution. Each of the N-1 simple circle zeros of the Fejér polynomial becomes a |u|^{2gamma} cusp under noninteger positive powers. The localized Fourier transform of this cusp, reconstructed by Laplace regularization/distributional derivatives and Taylor remainders, yields the stated exact Gamma/sin coefficient with O(m^{-2gamma-2}) fixed-parameter remainder. The nodal roots-of-unity DFT is real and sums to zero while its zero residue is positive. Its sign therefore forces infinitely many strictly negative coefficients for every noninteger gamma. A direct finite-Gram limit supplies a witness for nonpositive-type. Embedded standalone standard-library checker ran 313 finite diagnostics; they are supplementary.

value.rationale: Fejér and powered Fejér–Jackson kernels are canonical positive circular smoothing filters. This theorem determines precisely which continuous real-power parameter choices retain positive type across every finite point configuration, exposing spectral negativity invisible to pointwise positivity and to finite low-frequency checks. The exact modular Fourier-tail constants and infinitely recurring negative classes quantify a natural covariance/spectral-filter design boundary, going beyond the classical integer convolution observation.
